findings.assessment: Late accretion and second-generation catastrophic-impact origins are competing proposed interpretations, with geochemical/timing and density challenges explicitly discussed. Upper-layer18.5% porosity and mesosiderite-like mechanical mixtures are model interpretations, not local measured composition or a terrain map.

Radio Doppler primarily constrains gravity; ranging constrains heliocentric orbit; framing-camera landmarks constrain surface-relative orbit/rotation. Transfer-phase data were excluded because manoeuvre forces were strong. Instrument accuracy statements are publisher claims, not reproduced uncertainty for current imagery.

FC2SPC model uses about16500images across all phases; Approach/Survey establish prior shape, about75000 overlapping maplets and50m model from6.5m/20m images. Publisher50m model scale is not independently established resolution or identity of existing SPG map/DEM. COM-relative COF(.99,1.05,-.05)±.1km and best-fit ellipsoid284.62/277.24/226.33km versus spheroid280.89/226.32km are separate coordinate/model conventions, not catalogue-radius replacements.
ClaudiaDouble-Prime146degree meridian and non-principal-axis frame are specified. No rotation, shift or pole correction applied to current textures/DEM. No new angular/raster computation.

MONTE fits roughly2–10day arcs, local spacecraft/desaturation/stochastic acceleration/camera-pointing/calibration parameters, with global degree26gravity, constant pole, MOI scale, landmarks and heliocentric ephemeris. The paper attributes earlier Doppler/imaging landmark conflict to data calibration corrected during Ceres operations; this is an author account, not independent reproduction or diagnosis of Fidelity assets.

Three uniform-density layers, ellipsoidal mantle/core and hydrostatic-core assumptions constrain MCMC. Integrated autocorrelation convergence criterionchains>50tau is reported, not independently reproduced. Effective-density derivation assumes scaled layer shapes and restricts uncompensated topographic contribution; degree2order0 excluded for hydrostatic ellipsoidal-core assumption. None establishes unique physical layering, local chemistry, photometric calibration or map registration.

findings: Extended Data Table 1 distinguishes estimated parameters from shape-integrated homogeneous comparisons. Its spherical harmonic reference radius 265 km is a normalization convention, not a new catalogue physical radius. Footnote calls its uncertainties formal 1-sigma; this is distinct from main posterior 5–95 percentiles.
Table 1 gives normalized polar moment 0.4208 ± 0.0047 and constant-density shape value 0.4505. Pole/rotation solution and Claudia 146-degree convention have not been applied to Fidelity maps or DEM.

Extended Data Table 2 title says nutation parameters for normalized polar moment 0.4208, while its explanatory text says parameters are computed by numerical integration for constant-density Vesta at 0.4505 and fitted amplitudes scale inversely with C. Preserve this title/explanation distinction; no independent integration or implementation verification.

Extended Data Table 3 subset estimates: DSN LAMO only 0.4248 ± 0.0100; DSN all phases 0.4221 ± 0.0063; DSN plus optical LAMO 0.4173 ± 0.0068; DSN plus optical all phases CBE 0.4208 ± 0.0047; constrained gravity 16–26 0.4188 ± 0.0047. Author robustness interpretation is not an independently reproduced fit or image calibration.

Extended Data Table 4 prior bounds: volumetric mantle/core radii each 10–261.465 km, mantle/core densities each 2200–9000 kg/m3, palaeo-rotation 4.8–5.3 hours. Crust density computed to satisfy mass and constrained 1800–3600 kg/m3; density increases with depth, with additional layer thickness constraints. These are model priors, not measured layer radii, local chemistry or historical spin.
Page 11 supplies affiliations and correspondence, not additional observations.

Extended Data Figure 1 shows SPC topography relative to best-fit ellipsoid 284.62,277.24,226.33 km, with author-stated horizontal spatial resolution 100 m and height range -19.9 to 21.6 km. These printed conventions are not independently validated resolution or the existing SPG DEM reference sphere. Colours encode topography, not calibrated visible colour or chemistry.

Extended Data Figures 2–4 distinguish no-MOI constraint, MOI constraint, and MOI plus minimum crustal thickness 80 km. Captions explicitly use 5–95 percent quantile intervals; inset density distributions also show 1–99,10–90,25–75 bands. These model posterior choices must not be conflated with formal 1-sigma gravity uncertainties or direct interior geography.

Extended Data Figure 5 identifies FC2_00031311 as a Dawn Framing Camera HAMO-2 raw picture and overlays a rendered inset for Claudia reference at east longitude 146.000 degrees and latitude -1.662 degrees. This is an explicit paper reference, not a fetched/hashed raw product, an association with Bellicia PIA15384, or registration of Fidelity texture/DEM. No image acquisition timestamp is inferred.

Extended Data Figure 6 compares estimated gravity-solution landmark positions with prior SPC coordinates in Cartesian X,Y,Z. The authors interpret mean-zero differences as calibration consistency; this diagnostic has not been independently reproduced and does not calibrate Fidelity imagery, prove SPG/SPC byte identity, or authorize map shifts.
Title, eleven named authors, received 2023-11-27, accepted 2025-03-17, published 2025-04-23 and June 2025 issue are visually verified; these are publication history, not image acquisition dates.

Abstract frames limited density stratification and two possible origin scenarios as inference from updated moment of inertia, gravity and shape. Partial differentiation through late accretion versus impact-remnant/reaccretion are competing interpretations, not observed local chemistry or uniquely established history.

Figure 1 gravity/shape correlation and effective density spectra use modelling assumptions: shape errorless, topography nearly supported by gravity, and comparison curves with assumed crust thickness 50 km and mantle density 4000 kg/m3. These are not terrain colours, direct local density measurements, independently reproduced calibration or the existing SPG DEM product.

Page 2 distinguishes year-long Dawn orbital coverage, DSN Doppler Earth-relative line-of-sight speed, and onboard optical Vesta-relative spacecraft positions. A 265 km spherical harmonic normalization radius and Claudia Double-Prime frame are not new physical radius or permission to shift existing maps.

Authors state degree-26 solution sensitivity approximately degree20 and strong gravity/shape correlation to degree17. This does not independently validate individual native image geography, photometry or spatial resolution. Radau-Darwin hydrostatic assumptions are explicitly unsuitable for irregular, nonhydrostatic rapidly rotating Vesta.
